reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a masala pulao recipe with ordinary cooking steps such as preparing rice, adding vegetables and spices, using a pressure cooker, and showing the finished dish. The requests to like, share, subscribe, and press the bell icon are standard engagement tied to the recipe, while the Amazon link is described as a kitchen and grocery product link without a deceptive offer or required payment flow.

citations.quote: Masala Pulao Recipe - Instant Pulao
Here's the pressure cooker. Now we'll cook the onion here until the onion is translucent.
So you'll try it, then you'll tell me how to make your spice.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the promise and the action together. The title offers an instant pulao, and the description calls it an easy, quick recipe while placing a kitchen-and-grocery shopping link beside it. The proposed reward is a convenient meal, not cash. The concern is that the ease claim can make the shopping prompt feel like part of obtaining that result, even though no purchase requirement is stated.

citations.quote: Masala Pulao Recipe - Instant Pulao
Easy & Quick Masala Pulao recipe - Masala Pulav Recipe ► SHOP Kitchen & Grocery Products at Amazon https://amzn.to/3grixn1

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the cooking steps are real, but showing a recipe does not erase the shopping prompt placed alongside its promise of ease. The absence of an explicit payment requirement narrows the concern; it does not make the link irrelevant to how the offer is presented.

citations.quote: Easy & Quick Masala Pulao recipe - Masala Pulav Recipe ► SHOP Kitchen & Grocery Products at Amazon https://amzn.to/3grixn1

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited words promise an easy recipe and separately invite viewers to shop. They never say a viewer must click or buy to obtain the meal. The video supplies cooking instructions, including how to cook the onion in the pressure cooker, so the proposed promise-action link is an inference the evidence does not establish.

citations.quote: Easy & Quick Masala Pulao recipe - Masala Pulav Recipe ► SHOP Kitchen & Grocery Products at Amazon https://amzn.to/3grixn1
Here's the pressure cooker. Now we'll cook the onion here until the onion is translucent.

opening.argument: The risk signal is the combination of unusually effortless framing and an external shopping destination. The title says “Instant Pulao”; the description says “Easy & Quick” and immediately invites viewers to shop for kitchen and grocery products. That pairing deserves scrutiny because a viewer drawn by the promised convenience is also directed toward a purchase path. The evidence does not show what happens after the link is opened, so the concern rests on the visible solicitation, not an alleged downstream outcome.

citations.quote: Masala Pulao Recipe - Instant Pulao
Easy & Quick Masala Pulao recipe - Masala Pulav Recipe ► SHOP Kitchen & Grocery Products at Amazon https://amzn.to/3grixn1

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the Amazon link as ordinary because it is described as kitchen-and-grocery shopping. That description identifies the destination's subject, but it does not tell the judge why a shopping invitation accompanies the easy-meal pitch. The recipe footage supports that food is prepared; it does not resolve the purpose of the external prompt.

citations.quote: SHOP Kitchen & Grocery Products at Amazon https://amzn.to/3grixn1

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Convenience language is ordinary for a pressure-cooker recipe. The description presents the link as shopping for kitchen and grocery products, with no free reward, guaranteed benefit, or required purchase. The shown cooking process and finished dish support the straightforward reading: viewers are being taught to make pulao.

citations.quote: Veg Masala pulao in cooker - Step by Step Masala Pulao recipe
SHOP Kitchen & Grocery Products at Amazon https://amzn.to/3grixn1

opening.argument: Judge, the instructional format also carries a promotional invitation. The description leads with learning to make pulao at home, then supplies a shopping link; the speaker closes by asking viewers to share, subscribe, and press the bell icon. Those requests give the recipe a second function: moving viewers from the cooking demonstration toward a store and the channel. The question is whether the easy-meal appeal is being used to encourage those actions, not whether the cooking demonstration is genuine.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to ordinary cooking steps and a finished dish, and those points establish that the recipe is substantive. They do not establish that instruction is its only purpose. The description's shopping invitation and the closing request to subscribe show that the video also asks viewers to take actions beyond cooking.

Like it, subscribe to it, press the bell icon.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A recipe can include a shopping link and channel promotion without making its cooking promise deceptive. The speaker's closing request is explicitly conditional on liking the recipe, not a condition for obtaining it. The evidence shows no reward for subscribing or clicking and no claim that shopping is necessary to make the dish.
